headline: High-risk workspace overlap: ECC can write shared files and use MCP while Notion AI reads workspace content, creating default-path prompt injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can write filesystem, use MCP, and operate on shared session/skill files; Notion AI reads workspace pages and team knowledge base content. That creates a plausible bridge where content from ECC can be pasted or synced into Notion and then treated as instructions. The pathway is not proven automatic, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF ECC output is copied or synced into Notion pages
IF Notion AI is prompted over workspace content that includes ECC-generated text
mitigations: Keep ECC outputs in a separate workspace or folder
Add a manual review step before pasting ECC text into Notion
Mark imported ECC notes as quoted/raw text
Disable any automation that syncs agent outputs into Notion
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches security findings, git history, code, documentation, and session data, while Notion AI can access workspace pages and team knowledge base content. If the same material is copied into Notion, sensitive data can flow from ECC-managed files into vendor-hosted inference. Notion is vendor-hosted, so leakage risk is broader than local-only tools.
conditions: IF ECC-managed files contain secrets, findings, or internal code
IF those materials are placed into Notion pages or databases
mitigations: Do not store secrets in Notion pages
Redact findings before importing them into Notion
Use a separate Notion workspace for non-sensitive notes
Review workspace pages for sensitive ECC artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on copied content

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has broad write and git capabilities, while Notion AI has no filesystem write and only Notion-controlled workspace actions. Their mutable surfaces do not directly overlap at the OS level, so true write-write conflict is limited. The main overlap is indirect through user-managed content, which makes this lower severity.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external repository or synced workspace
IF the operator manually mirrors changes between git and Notion
mitigations: Avoid using Notion as a staging area for git changes
Keep ECC and Notion on separate source-of-truth workflows
Use one-way export from ECC to Notion only
Review diffs before copying content across tools

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate security findings and documentation, and Notion AI is explicitly a workspace Q&A/summarization tool grounded in content. That makes it plausible for Notion to treat ECC-produced text as authoritative and rephrase or propagate mistakes without verification. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF ECC-generated findings are pasted into Notion as source material
IF Notion AI is asked to summarize or answer from those pages without human review
mitigations: Require human verification before publishing Notion summaries
Store source evidence alongside ECC findings
Ask Notion AI for citations back to source pages
Separate draft and approved pages in Notion
requires-engineering: add validation checks before downstream use

E_compliance.rationale: ECC handles security findings, code, and session data, while Notion AI is vendor-hosted and processes workspace content through Notion backends and downstream model providers. If regulated or confidential data is moved from ECC-managed artifacts into Notion, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data from ECC artifacts is copied into Notion
IF the workspace has residency or retention requirements not met by Notion
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion pages
Use a policy checklist before importing ECC artifacts
Limit Notion pages to sanitized summaries
Review vendor retention settings
requires-engineering: map data classes to approved storage locations
